title: Class terms in the federal schedules carry the Controlled Substances Act definitions
subtopic: Defined terms in the schedule listings
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1300.01(a) ANY TERM NOT DEFINED IN 21 CFR PART 1300 SHALL HAVE THE DEFINITION SET FORTH IN SECTION 102 OF THE ACT, 21 U.S.C. 802, except that certain terms used in part 1316 are defined at the beginning of each subpart of that part. 21 U.S.C. 802(18) defines the term 'OPIATE' OR 'OPIOID' as ANY DRUG OR OTHER SUBSTANCE HAVING AN ADDICTION-FORMING OR ADDICTION-SUSTAINING LIABILITY SIMILAR TO MORPHINE OR BEING CAPABLE OF CONVERSION INTO A DRUG HAVING SUCH ADDICTION-FORMING OR ADDICTION-SUSTAINING LIABILITY. A schedule listing that uses such a term therefore reaches what the definition describes: 21 CFR 1308.12(b)(1) places in Schedule II 'opium and opiate, and any salt, compound, derivative, or preparation of opium or opiate', and then excludes named substances and their respective salts before listing the substances it includes.
exam_relevance: Tests that a schedule listing can reach a substance through a class term as well as by name, and that the class term is a legal definition keyed to addiction-forming or addiction-sustaining liability rather than a pharmacologic label.
exceptions: A term Part 1300 does define takes that definition, and certain terms used in 21 CFR part 1316 are defined at the beginning of each subpart of that part.
A class listing yields to the exclusions stated in its own paragraph, and to the preface directing that a listing applies unless the substance is specifically excepted or listed in another schedule.
common_confusions: Reading a class term in a listing as a pharmacologic description, such as activity at a receptor, rather than as the defined term the Act supplies.
Assuming every listing names its substances, when a listing may describe a class and then name the substances it excludes.
Taking an exclusion from one paragraph as an answer for the whole schedule, when another paragraph may reach the substance on its own terms.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1300.01(a) and 21 CFR 1308.12(b)(1) read on eCFR, current as of 2026-09-09, and 21 U.S.C. 802(18) read on uscode.house.gov, all on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
